Hi. Well... honestly, what made me finally call and come in today is... I just feel like the warm part of me completely shut off. I work as a stocker, filling orders all day, and it's a lot of being on my feet, moving boxes, you know, just exhausting work. So normally, the absolute best part of my day is coming home. I’d walk in, kick my work shoes off, and I usually just sit with my husband or try to watch my shows after work. We have this whole evening routine. And normally, I’d be so relieved, you know? I'd feel this sense of comfort, or even just a little happy to be done with the shift and just be there on the couch with him. 

But lately... I sit there, and I know I should feel comfort. I know I should feel a little happy, or anything at all, really. But there’s just nothing there. It's like I'm totally blank inside. And I try, I really do try to focus on the TV or whatever my husband is saying about his day, waiting for that warm, cozy feeling to come back, but it's just gone. It's just nothing. I've never been this way before, I've always been someone who really enjoys my quiet evenings and looks forward to them all day while I'm in the warehouse, and now it's just like I'm going through the motions but the feeling part is broken. I just don't know how to turn it back on, and it's really starting to bother me because I'm just sitting there feeling absolutely nothing when I know I'm supposed to be happy.

Sleep? Oh, it's... it's been terrible. Just absolutely awful. You know, I work the late shift, usually the 3:00 PM to 11:30 PM, sometimes going until midnight if we have a late truck coming in from the regional hub, and by the time I get home, I'm usually just bone tired. I mean, my feet ache, my back aches, and normally I would just wash my face, put on my pajamas—usually just an old t-shirt and some flannel pants—and I'd be out the second my head hit the pillow. I'll lie there in the dark, the room is quiet, the fan is on low just for the white noise, and I'll feel myself finally starting to drift off. You know that heavy feeling right before you fall asleep? I get right to that edge, and then... BAM. I jerk awake. My heart is pounding, my chest is tight, and I swear, I swear I can hear the sound of the wooden pallets shifting. That exact creaking, snapping sound they make right before they give way. It's so loud in my head that I'll actually sit up in bed and look around, even though I know I'm in my bedroom and not the warehouse. 

And this happens over and over. I'll drift off, hear the noise, jerk awake. Drift off, hear the noise, jerk awake. It's like my brain won't let my guard down. And on the rare occasions that I do manage to actually stay asleep for a few hours without waking up in a panic, it doesn't even matter. I'll wake up when my alarm goes off the next morning, and I feel like I haven't slept a wink. It's like I've been running a marathon all night instead of resting. My eyes are heavy, my body feels like lead, and I just... I never, ever feel rested anymore. It's just exhausting, being this exhausted all the time.

Enjoying time with my husband? I... honestly, that's a big part of why I finally decided I needed to come in and talk to someone. Because it's not just the sleep or the exhaustion. It's like... it's like the warm part of me just completely shut off. Like somebody went in and flipped a breaker, and all the lights went out in that section of my brain.

It's just... gone.

Moving slowly or having trouble sitting still? I... I don't think so. I mean, I know we just talked about how I feel heavy, like my arms and legs are made of lead, but I wouldn't say I'm actually moving slower. Like I said before, I still have to do my job. I still have to walk up and down the aisles, bend down to pick up the boxes, the small ones with the barcode on the side, the big ones that require a team lift. I'm still doing all of that at the same pace I always have. I have to, or else I wouldn't be able to keep up with the quota, and they track everything now, you know? They have these scanners that monitor how many items you pick per hour, and if you fall below a certain number, your supervisor gets an alert on their tablet, and then they come over and talk to you about "efficiency" and "time management." So I can't really afford to move slower, even if I feel like I'm dragging myself through mud. 

And as for sitting still... I don't think I'm having trouble with that, either. Like I was just saying about sitting on the couch with my husband, I just sit there. I don't feel restless or jittery or like I need to jump up and pace around the room. I just sit there on the couch, staring at the TV, feeling absolutely nothing. Sometimes I think I could sit there for hours and not even realize how much time has passed. It's almost like the opposite of not being able to sit still. It's like I'm glued to the spot, just stuck in this heavy, empty feeling. So, no, I wouldn't say I'm moving slower or having trouble sitting still. I'm just... existing in this weird, heavy void.

Activities I stopped doing? Activities I used to enjoy? Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I'm trying to think of what I even did for fun before all this happened. Honestly, between working full-time at the warehouse and trying to keep the house running, I didn't have a whole lot of hobbies to begin with. I mean, my husband and I, we have our routine. We order that, and then we sit on the couch and watch whatever shows we have recorded on the DVR for the week. Usually those home renovation shows, the ones where they buy a rundown house and completely gut it and fix it up in like, thirty minutes of television time. 

And we still do that. We ordered the pizza last Friday, exactly the same as always. We sat on the couch in the exact same spots—he always takes the side with the chaise lounge part so he can stretch his legs out, and I sit on the other side by the end table with the lamp. I didn't really care about what they were doing to the houses, like I wasn't invested in whether they chose the subway tile or the glass mosaic for the kitchen backsplash, but I sat there and watched it just like I always do. 

And on Saturdays, I usually do the grocery shopping in the morning. Yeah, my husband... that's... honestly, that's exactly what made me finally come in and talk to somebody. It's not just the warehouse. It's happening at home, too, but in a different way. 

Usually, when I get home from my shift, I take off my boots, leave them by the mudroom door so I don't track warehouse dirt everywhere, and my husband and I have this whole evening routine. I'm just going through the motions of sitting on the couch and watching TV, but the part of me that actually enjoys it, the part that feels joy or affection... it's just gone. And it's scaring me, because I keep trying to force myself to feel happy or relieved to be home, and I just can't find those feelings anywhere no matter how hard I dig for them.

It's like I'm glued to the spot, just stuck in this heavy, empty feeling. So, no, I wouldn't say I'm moving slower or having trouble sitting still. I'm just... existing in this weird, heavy void.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel like you're having trouble initiating activities or motivating yourself to do things?\n\nPatient: Trouble starting things? But I can tell just by the way my clothes fit that nothing has really changed. My work uniform for the warehouse—we have to wear these specific khaki cargo pants and a navy blue polo shirt with the company logo stitched on the left side—they still fit exactly the same as they always have. I still clasp my heavy leather belt on the exact same notch, the third hole from the end. \n\nI know sometimes when people go through something bad, they either stop eating completely or they eat everything in sight, you know, eating their feelings or whatever. I still have to walk up and down the aisles, bend down to pick up the boxes, the small ones with the barcode on the side, the big ones that require a team lift. I'm still doing all of that at the same pace I always have. I have to, or else I wouldn't be able to keep up with the quota, and they track everything now, you know? It's like I'm glued to the spot, just stuck in this heavy, empty feeling. So, no, I wouldn't say I'm moving slower or having trouble sitting still.
